messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm seeing steady memory growth on prod streaming-chat v2 when users run long tool-loop sessions (code-runner). Heap climbs ~180-220MB/hour per pod until OOM after ~8-12h. Not an immediate spike, more of a drift.

maria: Repro (local-ish): start a long streaming chat (~50k tokens across many turns) + repeated tool calls that return ~1-2KB outputs each. After ~3-4 hours of steady activity process RSS increases.

maria: Sample pmap output after 4h:```
PID  RSS
12345 5.1G
```
and jemalloc stats show allocated vs active diverging.

sameer: Do we have kv-cache residency logs per-session? Could be prefix/kv reuse holding references. Is this only streaming mode?

maria: Only reproduced on streaming+tool-loop. Non-streaming sessions with same total token count don't drift. Suspect streaming path keeps more KV slabs pinned (maybe due to partial KV copies for tool results).

olivia: Can you paste jemalloc stats (epoch/kernel) and kv slab map? I've seen fragmentation when slabs accumulate many small entries from tool outputs.

maria: Paste of jemalloc stats (abridged):```
jemalloc.stats
active: 4.9G
allocated: 3.3G
mapped: 6.2G
metadata: 200M

epoch: 1
chunks: ...
```
active >> allocated suggests internal fragmentation.

ken: I ran a sampler + heap prof on a repro run. Flamegraph shows many small allocations from KV serialization in stream loop: `kv_cache::insert_serialized_entry` and `streaming::append_chunk`. Also see repeated small blocks ~1-2KB.

ken: Quick grep of kv-residency metric:```
kv.resident_bytes.session[tool-loop]=+150MB over 3h
kv.bucket_count.high_fragmentation=46%
kv.evictions.failed_due_to_lock=3
```

olivia: Interesting — `evictions.failed_due_to_lock` means eviction attempted but couldn't reclaim because a session held the slab locked for streaming append. That would prevent reuse and cause new slabs to be allocated.

maria: Reproduced with `--kv-debug` enabled. Logs show repetitive pattern: `attempt_evict slab_id=42 -> locked, skip` then new slab allocated. Over time slabs accumulate.

sameer: Sounds like a contention bug in the streaming append path: we should avoid holding per-session slab locks across I/O. Maybe we moved to coarse-grained locks in last change for kernel selection refactor. @ken any PRs recently?

ken: I reverted the coarse lock in a local build and the repro run stops drifting. With fine-grained per-bucket CAS we see evictions proceed normally. There's a PR from 1789009876 that changed lock granularity during kernel selection scheduling; might be related.

olivia: Two quick mitigations to deploy while we triage: 1) force periodic background compaction that tries to `force_evict` ignoring session locks after a timeout (safe fallback), 2) add an opt-in config to disable prefix-level caching for tool-loop sessions to reduce small-entry churn.

maria: I'm +1 on both. For 1) can we implement short-circuit: if slab hasn't been accessed for X secs and eviction failed N times, mark it for asynchronous eviction by background thread (no blocking on session lock)?

ken: We need to be careful with correctness (can't evict in-use KV segments that are actively read). We can add a `try_acquire_for_reclaim` that fails fast unless lock owner indicates idle. Streaming session could set an idle bit when waiting for I/O.

sameer: Also let's add telemetry: per-slab allocation_time, last_access_time, failed_evictions counter, and per-session slab_refs. We'll graph these and set alert if resident_bytes grows >100MB in 1h for a pod.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: canary job queued for `kv-fallback-evict` feature branch. CI shows green.

maria: Quick patch diff I used locally (pseudo):```diff
- auto lock = slab.lock();
- append_chunk(...);
+ if (!slab.try_lock_for_append()) {
+   serialize_to_temp_and_append_nonblocking(...);
+ } else {
+   append_chunk(...);
+ }
```
This reduced failed evictions to 0 in my runs.

ken: Great. We'll open a bug (INF-5232) to track root cause + revert plan. Action items:
- sameer: add slab/gc telemetry + alert (ETA 48h)
- olivia: implement background compaction fallback (ETA 24-36h)
- ken: audit recent kernel-selection/lock PRs and prepare revert/patch (ETA 24h)
- maria: run extended canary (12h) and attach heap profiles (ETA 24h)

maria: I'll also add an automated repro harness that simulates streaming+tool-loop load with slower tool responses to force lock contention. Will share links.

sameer: If canary looks good we can roll the background compaction to prod config as a stopgap. Long-term we want to fix lock logic.

olivia: One more thought — consider shrinking slab size for tool-loop sessions via routing policy: route tool-heavy sessions to smaller-slab pools so fragmentation impact is bounded. Might be a quick mitigation for high-traffic customers.

maria: Good idea. I'll add a routing flag to the repro harness and test.

ken: Logged INF-5232 with stack traces and sample heap profile in the ticket.

maria: Thanks all. Will post updates in this thread and link the ticket. :thumbsup:
